root_cause.text: The vsock virtio receive coalescing logic in virtio_transport_recv_enqueue() incorrectly assumed small RX sk_buffs were always linear, so after MSG_ZEROCOPY introduced non-linear skbs it copied from a non-linear skb as if payload were in the linear data area.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “Since the introduction of MSG_ZEROCOPY support, assumption that a small skb will always be linear is incorrect. In the zerocopy case, data is lost and the linear skb is appended with uninitialized kernel memory,” and the patch fixes this by adding `&& !skb_is_nonlinear(skb)` before attempting coalescence.

In the zerocopy case, data is lost and the linear skb is appended with uninitialized kernel memory,” and the patch fixes this by adding `&& !skb_is_nonlinear(skb)` before attempting coalescence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip non-linear SKBs in virtio receive small-packet coalescing to avoid mishandling zerocopy payload storage.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the small-packet coalescing path in virtio_transport_recv_enqueue() was extended by adding `&& !skb_is_nonlinear(skb)`, and the accompanying comment was updated to state that non-linear SKBs (such as zerocopy ones) are skipped because their payload is carried in `skb_shinfo`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the optimization that copies small incoming packets into the buffer of the last queued packet now runs only for linear SKBs. This prevents the code from attempting to treat non-linear or zerocopy SKBs as if their payload were stored in the main data area, avoiding incorrect payload handling during receive queue enqueueing.

grouping_result.intent: Skip non-linear SKBs in virtio receive small-packet coalescing to avoid mishandling zerocopy payload storage.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by preventing receive coalescing from treating non-linear SKBs as small linear buffers, which is exactly the incorrect assumption introduced as problematic with MSG_ZEROCOPY.

candidates.rationale: This condition initiates small-packet coalescing based only on length and queue state, implicitly assuming such small SKBs are safe to copy from directly. The vulnerability is that it omitted any check that the incoming skb was linear, allowing non-linear zerocopy SKBs to enter the coalescing path and be copied as if payload were in the linear area.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gates the small-packet receive coalescing path using only packet length and queue state. It omitted any requirement that the incoming skb be linear, which caused non-linear zerocopy skbs to enter code that copied data as though it resided in the linear data area.
